sn48.58:1.1: This is famously the scene of Sāriputta’s awakening ([mn74:1.2]()).
sn48.58:1.3: The interpretation of this discourse is problematic, for reasons I shall explain below. However, I believe it is thematically similar to [sn16.5](), where Mahākassapa explains that he continues his austere lifestyle even though he is enlightened both because he enjoys it, and to inspire future generations. The current text seems corrupt, and no parallels are recorded. | I take the expression _pavattamāno pavattati_ (“in rolling forth, roll forth”) as referring to Sāriputta’s role as the disciple who, like no other, continues to “roll forth” the wheel of the teaching ([mn111:23.1](), [sn8.7:3.4](), [an1.187:1.1]()). The Buddha is asking what motivates Sāriputta to teach.
sn48.58:1.4: And the answer is that it’s of benefit for the enlightenment of others, although this is not made clear. It is, I think, supported by the conclusion of the sutta, where Sariputta mentions a set of dhammas that elsewhere are said to be for the long lasting of the sasana. BB translates this and following passages as “considering as benefit the …” thus seemingly translating atthavasam, but it is absent.
sn48.58:2.1: text seems corrupt, the indriyas are not enlightenment …
sn48.58:3.2: Five things leading to non-decline of the dispensation.
